title: Opal Manufacturing: Edge Inference Sweep and Cost-Latency Playbook
content:
Executive summary:

This is a working sweep report and playbook from the Opal Manufacturing on-site workshop (2029-03-12). Goal: identify a deployable inference configuration for a plant-edge quality-assurance service that balances 95th/99th percentile latency constraints (<=150ms p95 for short inference, <=600ms p95 for batch inspection) and cost targets (<$25 per 1M tokens equivalent for steady-state). We tested three hardware classes (H100-80GB, A10G, and L4), two quantization modes (fp16 and int8/awq-lite), and three runtime profiles (single-request, micro-batched, and prefix-cached).

Scope and constraints:
- Model: distilled instruction-tuned 7B variant (sequence len 1–512 typical; imagery-derived metadata + short prompts).
- Typical request: 40 tokens in, 80 tokens out (avg 120 tokens per inference).
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 150ms for 95% of inference types (low-latency QA) and p95 <= 600ms for bulk inspection mode with batching.
- Cost target: <$25 per 1M tokens served under steady-state 200 qps workload typical in one plant.
- Network: on-prem private deployment (VPC) with modest egress; need fallback to hosted for spikes.

Methodology:
- Workload generator: poisson arrival baseline with scheduled microbursts (100ms bursts every 30s) and larger maintenance bursts (3–5s every 2 hours) to emulate conveyor spikes.
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, tail latency distribution, CPU/GPU utilization, token/sec, completed qps, cold-starts, cache hit rate for KV prefix cache, memory footprint.
- Runs: each config executed for 30 minutes steady-state after a 10-minute warmup; microburst sweeps included in a second 30-minute stage.

Key findings (high level):
- H100 + int8 (awq-lite) gave the best cost-to-latency tradeoff: p95 ~ 110ms at 200 qps when micro-batching disabled; with micro-batching (batch size 8) throughput increased 2.8x while p95 rose to ~220ms (still acceptable for bulk mode).
- A10G fp16 delivered acceptable latency at lower throughput: p95 ~ 170ms at 120 qps (single-request), but becomes cost-inefficient above 150 qps due to less memory headroom for KV caching and smaller effective batch sizes.
- L4 (edge GPU) can serve low qps (<40 qps) with p95 ~ 320ms single-request; good as a very low-cost per-site option but not for plant-wide 200 qps traffic.
- KV prefix caching reduced mean token compute by ~18% for repeating templates, reducing p95 by ~12% across configs after warmup. Cache-warmup time ~8–12 minutes depending on traffic locality.
- Cold-starts on private nodes (scale-up events) were the dominant cause of p99 spikes (up to 1.8s). Autoscaler cooldown and pre-warm policies reduce observed p99 spikes by ~60%.

Representative numbers (steady-state, 200 qps, 120 tokens/inference):
- H100 fp16 single-request: p50 60ms, p95 160ms, p99 310ms, throughput 210 qps, cost est $22.4 / 1M tokens.
- H100 int8 (awq-lite) single-request: p50 48ms, p95 110ms, p99 200ms, throughput 240 qps, cost est $15.8 / 1M tokens.
- H100 int8 batched (b=8): p50 55ms, p95 220ms, p99 420ms, throughput 660 qps, cost est $9.1 / 1M tokens (for bulk inspection mode).
- A10G fp16 single-request: p50 80ms, p95 170ms, p99 360ms, throughput 125 qps, cost est $26.7 / 1M tokens.
- L4 int8 single-request: p50 180ms, p95 320ms, p99 740ms, throughput 38 qps, cost est $48.3 / 1M tokens (per-site low throughput case).

Interpretation and tradeoffs:
- For plant-wide steady traffic at ~200 qps with latency-sensitive QA checks, H100 with int8 AWQ-lite is the recommended primary profile. It meets the p95 budget and comes in under the cost target.
- For bulk offline inspection windows where latency can be relaxed, enable micro-batching aggressively on H100 to minimize token cost—this pushes cost down by ~42% versus single-request int8 baseline but increases p95, so schedule bulk jobs to tolerance windows.
- A10G is a good compromise for medium plants (80–150 qps) when H100 capacity is constrained, but operationally we recommend Dedicated bursts to H100 for peak windows.
- L4 devices are only recommended for very small satellite inspection kiosks; do not use as primary host for aggregated plant-level traffic without sharding and request routing.

Operational recommendations (deployment playbook):
1) Dedicated cluster: reserve 2 H100 instances per plant region with autoscaler headroom (1 warm spare) and pre-warm policy during shift changes. Enable int8 awq-lite quantization profile.
2) Fallbacks: route to A10G pool if H100 capacity crossed threshold; enable model-variant fallback (fp16 smaller model) for graceful degradation.
3) Cache policy: enable prefix/KV cache for templated prompts; set cache TTL 12h and async background refresh during low-load windows.
4) Batching policy: default single-request low-latency route; bulk inspection route uses dynamic batching with target batch size 8–16 and max latency 600ms.
5) Monitoring & alerts: p95 > 180ms alert for low-latency route; p99 > 1s alert for any route. Track cold-start counts and autoscaler events.
6) Cost controls: enforce per-route cost caps and token throttles during sustained >300 qps spikes to prevent runaway spend.

Open questions and next steps:
- Quantization fidelity: need a short eval on mislabeled QA cases at int8 awq-lite vs fp16 with live prompt set (we saw a 0.8–1.6% drop on a 1.2k-case eval, but that needs business validation). Owner: Maya.
- Autoscaler tuning: evaluate pre-warm + predictive scale-up at 10-minute granularity around shift handovers. Owner: Diego.
- Hosted fallback latency: run 2-week smoke on hosted fallback during spikes to quantify additional end-to-end network cost and SLO delta. Owner: Arjun.

Action items (owners / ETA):
- Maya: run fidelity eval (int8 vs fp16) on 1.2k prioritized prompts, report by 2029-03-29.
- Diego: implement pre-warm autoscaler policy and simulate shift-change workload by 2029-04-05.
- Arjun: create fallback playbook and hosted fallthrough sim, finish by 2029-04-12.
- Nina: produce deployment RFC for Dedicated cluster config with fallbacks and cost caps, draft by 2029-03-28.

Notes to self / informal findings:
- Batch-size sweet spot depends heavily on response-token variance; for sequences with high variance, cap batch size to avoid p99 amplification.
- Cache warmup is non-linear: the first 2 minutes of traffic give disproportionately high hits for common templates. Consider short warmup scripts when deploying model upgrades.
- Slack threads: #plant-opal and #solutions-discuss contain raw traces (see linked artifacts).

Appendix (short runbook snippets):
- Quick rollback: route 100% traffic to fp16 smaller model variant, drain worker pool, unschedule batch windows.
- Warm-start script: pre-populate prefix cache using recent week’s prompt set and synthetic variations (script in linked repo PR 412).

This document is a working draft and will be iterated after the fidelity eval and autoscaler tuning runs. Comments inline welcome — particularly from product and ops on acceptable p95 thresholds for bulk vs QA modes.
